module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum

@[expose] public section

noncomputable def Matrix.IsHermitian.maxEigenvalue {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) : ℝ :=
  iSup hA.eigenvalues

findings.description: Independent defect found at the sole direct library use site, FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/LovaszTheta.lean:39–42, not in maxEigenvalue itself. The definition minimizes the largest eigenvalue over symmetric matrices with diagonal entries 1 and entries 0 on edges. This returns 1 for every nonempty finite graph: the identity is feasible and has largest eigenvalue 1, while every feasible matrix has trace equal to the number of vertices, hence largest eigenvalue at least 1. Thus the two-vertex edgeless graph gets value 1 instead of its standard Lovász theta number 2. The general constant-value assertion is proved without sorry in /workspace/review/theta_checks.lean. No current problem declaration uses this definition.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lov%C3%A1sz_number, “Equivalent expressions”: the eigenvalue-minimization formulation ranges over symmetric matrices with a_ij = 1 whenever i = j or the vertices are not adjacent; entries on edges are unrestricted. “Value for well-known graphs” gives θ(\overline{K_n}) = n. The distinct dual formulation has zero entries on edges, but maximizes the sum of entries of a positive-semidefinite matrix with trace 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the eigenvalue infimum, but replace the admissibility conditions by `∀ i j, ¬ G.Adj i j → A i j = 1`. This includes the diagonal because a SimpleGraph has no loops; edges must remain unrestricted. Update the docstring accordingly and remove its positive-semidefiniteness requirement, which is not part of this formulation. Merely adding positive semidefiniteness to the current definition would still give the constant value 1.

reformulations.difference: Uses a real indexed supremum of Mathlib's eigenvalue enumeration rather than explicitly selecting the largest eigenvalue.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nonempty finite index type, Mathlib proves that the range of hA.eigenvalues is exactly spectrum ℝ A. This range is finite and nonempty, so its real supremum is attained and is its greatest element. In /workspace/review/spectrum_checks.lean I proved `hA.maxEigenvalue = r ↔ IsGreatest (spectrum ℝ A) r` for arbitrary RCLike scalars and nonempty finite index types. I also proved agreement with `sSup (spectrum ℝ A)` for every index type, including the empty case.

review.notes: No misformalization was found in the requested Spectrum.lean file itself; the finding is explicitly an independent error in its direct library consumer. Checked empty and zero matrices, a negative singleton, and two-dimensional diagonal matrices with negative and mixed-sign eigenvalues. On an empty index type maxEigenvalue returns 0, following Mathlib's real-supremum totalization; the spectrum is empty. This does not produce a discovered problem-statement error, and the graph consumer also returns 0 on the empty vertex type. Neither maxEigenvalue nor lovaszThetaFunction is referenced by a problem declaration. The final Lean checks compile and their named results depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. No repository files were edited.

not_fixed.reason: Defined in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/LovaszTheta.lean, which is outside the permitted edit scope. The fix requires changing its matrix constraints to `∀ i j, ¬ G.Adj i j → A i j = 1` and correcting its docstring. There is no corresponding change needed in Spectrum.lean.

submission.summary: No files were modified. Spectrum.lean contains only the correctly defined maxEigenvalue; changing it would not legitimately repair the graph definition. The required compilation completed with no errors or warnings.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported defect requires editing LovaszTheta.lean, but only Spectrum.lean may be edited. There is no valid in-file portion of this fix.
